title: Is a Virus Alive? Viruses Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Diya has a bad cold and asks for an antibiotic, but the doctor says no: antibiotics act on bacteria, and a cold is caused by a virus. So what is a virus, and is it even alive?

We follow how viruses were found (Ivanowsky 1892, Beijerinek 1898 and contagium vivum fluidum, Stanley 1935), see why a virus is inert outside a cell but an obligate parasite inside one, and zoom from a mosaic tobacco leaf into a leaf cell, the tobacco mosaic virus and its capsid of capsomeres around RNA. Then the rules of virus structure (helical or polyhedral, RNA or DNA but never both), a bacteriophage taking over a bacterium step by step, which nucleic acid plant, bacterial and animal viruses carry, the diseases they cause, a worked example labelling TMV and a bacteriophage, the exam trap, an original NEET match-the-following question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 18 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
